perspective:
Alice Lim’s accessible information:

- Alice knows Austin as an old high-school friend; they are close and regularly discuss personal and professional lives. She knows her own work as a dental hygienist and understands Austin works in an insurance/office setting.
- She observed Austin becoming reserved when work came up. She invited him to coffee and asked if work was okay. Austin told her it was nothing, just usual ups and downs, and that he wasn’t sure how to handle a few complicated things at work. Alice suspected he might be hiding something about his job performance, but Austin did not confirm this.
- After that conversation, Alice believed Austin might be considering a career change due to dissatisfaction and felt worried about him. She asked if he had thought about changing careers and suggested healthcare. Austin said he had thought about it but didn’t know what other paths to take and asked for suggestions. Alice offered to tell him about healthcare and connect him with contacts. Austin said it sounded interesting and wanted to know more about her experiences and what it involves.
- Alice sensed Austin was hesitant about changing careers because of fear of the unknown; she felt frustration and empathy. She told him about her friend Lara, who switched to healthcare in her late 30s and was happier. Austin said that was inspiring but worried about risks and the initial struggle. Alice encouraged him, saying growth comes from stepping out of comfort zones, and that she supports him. Austin thanked her and said her support and success stories helped.
- Seeing Austin’s openness, Alice felt encouraged and hopeful. She suggested he talk to a career counselor and offered to connect him with friends in healthcare for a clearer picture. Austin agreed and appreciated the connections. Alice said she would set up a meeting next week; Austin thanked her and looked forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings she participated in, Alice believed Austin was ready to take the next steps and appreciated her help; she felt satisfaction and joy. She told him she was proud and asked how he felt. Austin said he was excited, a bit nervous, and mostly grateful. Alice suggested regular check-ins; Austin agreed, saying it would keep him focused and that he valued her perspective.

Alice does not have access to any hidden job-performance details, private reasons, or definitive career-change decisions beyond what Austin stated and what she observed.
